title: AST SpaceMobile Is 78% Below Its High and Pushed Its Launch Target to 2027. Here’s the Exact Price Where I’d Finally Buy.
author: Leo Sun
description: AST SpaceMobile's stock has plummeted 78% from its May 2026 high of $133.09 to $29 per share due to delayed satellite launches pushed to 2027 and competition from SpaceX's $8 billion spectrum acquisition. The analyst suggests the stock could fall to the mid-teens during a market crash but would be a long-term buy at those levels, given projected revenue growth to $1.65 billion by 2028.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock has declined 78% from its high due to delayed launches to 2027 and increased competition from SpaceX's spectrum acquisition. However, the analyst sees potential for long-term recovery based on projected revenue growth.

title: Can AT&T's New Apple Device Deals Strengthen Its Subscriber Growth?
author: Na
description: AT&T is launching aggressive holiday promotions offering the iPhone 18 Pro for $0 with trade-ins, up to $1,200 off select devices, and $1,900 in bundle savings. The company is also incentivizing provider switches with up to $800 toward device payoffs. These initiatives aim to attract new subscribers and improve retention while competing with Verizon and T-Mobile's similar holiday offerings.

title: SpaceX's New Deal with Qualcomm Aims to Take on Mobile Carriers. History Says It's Going to Be an Uphill Battle.
author: Chris Neiger
description: SpaceX announced a partnership with Qualcomm to launch Starlink Mobile, a new cellular carrier service to compete with AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile. While history suggests this is a difficult challenge—as previous fourth carriers like Boost Mobile failed—SpaceX has advantages including an established 13.6 million Starlink subscriber base, potential acquisition of Boost Mobile, and proven ability to scale internet services profitably.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: SpaceX has significant growth potential with Starlink Mobile and strong existing subscriber base, but faces substantial competitive headwinds from entrenched carriers and uncertain capital expenditure requirements that could pressure stock price.
Qualcomm benefits from providing network infrastructure and technology (Dragonwing) to SpaceX's new venture, representing a significant revenue opportunity from a major customer.

title: T vs. VZ: Which Telecom Stock is a Better Investment Right Now?
author: Na
description: Verizon is positioned as a more compelling investment than AT&T, driven by stronger cash flow growth (24.4%), improving subscriber trends, and strategic initiatives like the Frontier acquisition and Google AI data center agreement. While AT&T benefits from fiber expansion and broadband growth, it faces challenges from rising debt levels and promotional pricing pressures that limit its investment appeal.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong cash flow growth of 24.4%, improving postpaid phone net additions, expanding fiber footprint through Frontier acquisition, $1 billion Google AI data center agreement, record adjusted EBITDA of $13.7 billion, and disciplined financial execution make it the preferred investment choice.

While AT&T shows growth opportunities through fiber expansion (39.7 million locations, targeting 60 million by 2030) and strong Advanced Connectivity revenue growth (23.4%), it faces significant headwinds including rising net debt ($149.82 billion), increased debt-to-EBITDA ratio (3.13), and promotional pricing pressures that offset pricing benefits.
